For self\\u2011serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign\\u2011up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).\\n\\n2) Default retention windows (hosted API)\\n- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.\\n- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.\\n- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.\\n- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine\\u2011tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.\\n\\n3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines\\n- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. For customers who require EU\\u2011only custody we ensure backups remain in\\u2011region; cross\\u2011region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.\\n- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.\\n\\n5) Key management & auditability\\n- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer\\u2011managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.\\n- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Main points to confirm:

    "From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Olga — draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.

1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self‑serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign‑up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.
- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.
- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.
- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine‑tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.

3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines
- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.
- Backups / long‑term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross‑region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.

4) Backups & cross‑region replication
- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU‑only custody we ensure backups remain in‑region; cross‑region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.

5) Key management & auditability
- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer‑managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.
- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Logs include the user, timestamp, object id, and operation status.

Notes on evidence: I attached the small residency matrix and architecture diagram if they want an appendix entry. Suggest we offer Crestline the EU tenancy addendum and a 30‑day primary purge / 90‑day backup scrub cadence in writing; that should be acceptable for their board.

If that reads OK, Olga, happy for you to send to Emma.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Product
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-arch.pdf

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the SQ. Please find our short answers below; I’ve attached a one‑page summary and the draft responses for inclusion in your packet. If your board needs tighter timelines, we can add the EU tenancy addendum and a CMK option to the order form.

Summary answers (for packet)
• Storage location: Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy’s primary region. Self‑serve accounts default to the nearest regional cluster (US by default); EU‑only tenancy pinning is available under enterprise contract.
• Default retention: Request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default (configurable to 90/365 for enterprise). Embeddings retained 14 days by default (can be reduced to 7 days). Model snapshots retained until deleted; rolling snapshot retention default 30 days.
• Erasure timelines: Primary data purge within 30 days after a verified erasure request or tenant termination. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days; we provide a deletion attestation on completion.
• Backups & replication: Backups may replicate to a secondary region for DR depending on SLA; for EU‑only contracts cross‑region replication is disabled. Max default backup retention 90 days (extendable by agreement).
• KMS & audit: Encryption at rest via cloud KMS by default; enterprise customers may use customer‑managed keys or HSMs. Deletion/erasure events are logged in the audit trail (365‑day retention) and can be surfaced in the console or delivered as an export for enterprise customers.

Attachments: crestline_answers_v1.docx (draft answers), data-residency-matrix.xlsx, redwood-hosted-arch.pdf

Next steps: If that looks good I’ll send a formal addendum for EU tenancy pinning and CMK options. Otherwise send any edits and we’ll update the doc.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Solutions - CSM Escalations
Redwood Inference

    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"architecture\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"3478920001\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"3478920001\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"3478921234\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"alex_k\",\n    \"maria_dev\",\n    \"sam_ops\",\n    \"patrick_arch\",\n    \"elena_pm\",\n    \"deploy-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"text\": \"alex_k: quick RFC follow-up: sketched a minimal control-plane swap flow to respect data residency during failover.\\n\\nmaria_dev: how do we handle in-flight requests with KV cache refs?\\n\\nalex_k: two paths: 1) drain+proxy shadowing until KV TTLs expire (fast), 2) synchronous lease handoff (slow but consistent). preferring drain+proxy with consent checks.\\n\\nsam_ops: proxy forwarding may violate residency. need a consent gate.\\n\\nalex_k: agreed. proxy only forwards if tenant.cross_region_consent=true. otherwise 409 + Retry-After and operator signal.\\n\\npatrick_arch: make consent a tenant config in control-plane so routers can cache it.\\n\\nmaria_dev: streaming needs special handling. allow pinned streams to finish locally; mirror audit logs.\\n\\nelena_pm: product: surface three admin modes: no-forward, consent-forward, emergency-consent. customers choose outage vs forwarding.\\n\\nalex_k: control-plane API: PATCH /tenants/:id with resource_version for optimistic concurrency.\\n\\nmaria_dev: yes, include tenant.resource_version to avoid races.\\n\\nalex_k: headers: X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal, X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown.\\n\\nsam_ops: unknown -> deny by default. ops can authorize emergency-consent (two-person approval, timebound).\\n\\npatrick_arch: long-term: split lease metadata into a lightweight \\\"assertor\\\" service that answers is_writable(tenant,region) <5ms P95. it subscribes to control-plane events.\\n\\nmaria_dev: bootstrap/partition: assertor caches with TTL. if control-plane unreachable and cache expired, proxies default to conservative deny.\\n\\ndeploy-bot: canary started: assertor v1.0 -> 10% traffic. alert if p95 > 50ms or error-rate > 0.5%.\\n\\nalex_k: next steps: short RFC PR with tenant states, PATCH shape, assertor contract, proxy header semantics. ping me for quick review.\\n\\npatrick_arch: will review.\\n\\nmaria_dev: I'll add tests for state transitions and header propagation.\\n\\nelena_pm: I'll draft UI copy and customer docs for the three modes and emergency workflow.\\n\\nalex_k: thanks, posting PR link shortly. :rocket:\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"text\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "architecture",
  "thread_ts": "3478920001",
  "first_message_ts": "3478920001",
  "last_message_ts": "3478921234",
  "participants": [
    "alex_k",
    "maria_dev",
    "sam_ops",
    "patrick_arch",
    "elena_pm",
    "deploy-bot"
  ],
  "text": "alex_k: quick RFC follow-up: sketched a minimal control-plane swap flow to respect data residency during failover.

maria_dev: how do we handle in-flight requests with KV cache refs?

alex_k: two paths: 1) drain+proxy shadowing until KV TTLs expire (fast), 2) synchronous lease handoff (slow but consistent). preferring drain+proxy with consent checks.

sam_ops: proxy forwarding may violate residency. need a consent gate.

alex_k: agreed. proxy only forwards if tenant.cross_region_consent=true. otherwise 409 + Retry-After and operator signal.

patrick_arch: make consent a tenant config in control-plane so routers can cache it.

maria_dev: streaming needs special handling. allow pinned streams to finish locally; mirror audit logs.

elena_pm: product: surface three admin modes: no-forward, consent-forward, emergency-consent. customers choose outage vs forwarding.

alex_k: control-plane API: PATCH /tenants/:id with resource_version for optimistic concurrency.

maria_dev: yes, include tenant.resource_version to avoid races.

alex_k: headers: X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal, X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown.

sam_ops: unknown -> deny by default. ops can authorize emergency-consent (two-person approval, timebound).

patrick_arch: long-term: split lease metadata into a lightweight "assertor" service that answers is_writable(tenant,region) <5ms P95. it subscribes to control-plane events.

maria_dev: bootstrap/partition: assertor caches with TTL. if control-plane unreachable and cache expired, proxies default to conservative deny.

deploy-bot: canary started: assertor v1.0 -> 10% traffic. alert if p95 > 50ms or error-rate > 0.5%.

alex_k: next steps: short RFC PR with tenant states, PATCH shape, assertor contract, proxy header semantics. ping me for quick review.

patrick_arch: will review.

maria_dev: I'll add tests for state transitions and header propagation.

elena_pm: I'll draft UI copy and customer docs for the three modes and emergency workflow.

alex_k: thanks, posting PR link shortly. :rocket:",

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json",
    "title": "add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"30211\",\n  \"title\": \"add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway\",\n  \"author\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-03\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2026-02-03\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/security/kms-residency-assertor\",\n  \"description\": \"Motivation: customers with mixed-region deployments required deterministic KMS routing while preserving auditable, append-only commitments for cross-region fallback. This PR introduces a lightweight per-tenant residency assertor, an operator-configurable KMS operator allowlist, and an \\\"audit commitment gateway\\\" that signs short commitment records for any request that is routed off-region or to a fallback key.\\n\\nWhat it does: Adds a residency assertor that derives a tenant region preference from (in order) tenant metadata, residency claim headers, and recent routing history (sticky hints). When explicit tenancy region is missing, the assertor emits a deterministic candidate list rather than a single decision to enable safe canary rollouts. KMS selection now consults an allowlist and a staged preference table; if the chosen KMS is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and forwarded through the audit commitment gateway, which atomically records a signed commitment (SHA256 -> operator KMS sign) and returns a short commitment id that is stored in the request audit trail.\\n\\nRollout plan: feature is gated behind feature flag \\\"residency_assertor_v1\\\" with three rollout modes: disabled, observe-only (assertions emitted to audit but not enforced), and enforce. We will start in observe-only across a small percentage of traffic, then flip to enforce for specific enterprise tenants. Backwards compatible: if not enabled, runtime behavior is unchanged.\\n\\nConfiguration: new Helm values documented under deploy/helm/redwood-private/values-residency.yaml. Operators can configure: operator_kms_allowlist (ARNs), fallback_policy (prefer-nearest|prefer-cost|consent-first), commit_signer_key (service principal), and audit_holdback_window_seconds (short buffer window used by commitment gateway for transient redaction requests).\\n\\nSecurity and compliance notes: commitments are signed by a dedicated signing key stored in the operator KMS; commitments include a compact mutation-proof vector (timestamp + request-hash + origin-region) to support later non-repudiable verification. Audit-forwarder retains commitment IDs and can fetch the signed commitment for external compliance queries. Access to the commitment verification endpoint is RBAC-protected via a new v2 policy template.\\n\\nTesting and validation: added unit tests for deterministic candidate ordering, a simulation harness to exercise cross-region fallback under random failure, and an integration test that verifies the signed commitment roundtrip against the operator KMS emulator. Performance overhead measured at ~0.6ms median added latency in observe-only mode, 1.8ms in enforce mode for off-region fallbacks.\\n\\nMigration / Operational guidance: operators should seed operator_kms_allowlist before enabling enforce mode; enable observe-only for 72 hours and review audit commitments using the console (Audit -> Commitments view). We include a small migration script to backfill missing residency hints from a 30-day routing history.\\n\\nRelated: Linked Linear ENG-4123 (residency policy), PM-982 (enterprise residency product work). Addresses support ticket SUP-2345 about inconsistent KMS selection for EU-regulated tenants.\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"b6f3c9e: add ResidencyAssertor interface and initial implementation\",\n    \"d12a7f1: introduce AuditCommitmentGateway and signing flow\",\n    \"9a4b1cc: operator allowlist config and KMS selection policy\",\n    \"e7f2cbc: helm values and docs for residency config\",\n    \"4d8a910: integration tests and performance microbench harness\",\n    \"c2b3d55: add RBAC v2 policy template for commitment verification endpoint\",\n    \"f19e2aa: migration backfill script and admin console hooks\"\n  ],\n  \"files_changed\": [\n    \"server/kms/residency_assertor.go\",\n    \"server/audit/commitment_gateway.go\",\n    \"server/kms/selection_policy.go\",\n    \"pkg/rbac/v2/policies/commitment_verifier_policy.yaml\",\n    \"deploy/helm/redwood-private/values-residency.yaml\",\n    \"docs/security/kms-residency.md\",\n    \"tests/integration/test_residency_assertor.py\",\n    \"tools/migrations/backfill_residency_hints.py\"\n  ],\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"8\",\n  \"additions\": \"1286\",\n  \"deletions\": \"214\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Arjun Patel\",\n    \"Lucia Gomez\",\n    \"Samir Rao\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"security\",\n    \"compliance\",\n    \"kms\",\n    \"rbac\",\n    \"runtime\",\n    \"performance\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-4123\",\n    \"PM-982\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_jira\": [\n    \"SUP-2345\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"ci_checks\": [\n    \"unit-tests: pass\",\n    \"integration-tests: pass\",\n    \"lint: pass\",\n    \"e2e-residency: pass (flaky on last run, rerun passed)\",\n    \"security-scan: pass\"\n  ],\n  \"review_comments\": \"Arjun: Requested a clearer failure mode when the commit signer is unavailable; asked to add metrics for commit gateway failures.\\nAuthor(Maya): Added an exponential backoff and a new metric audit.commitments.failures, documented behavior in the helm values.\\nLucia: Asked for RBAC policy language to limit access to the verification endpoint to tenant-auditors only; requested unit test for policy generation.\\nAuthor: Added commitment_verifier_policy.yaml and unit tests.\\nSamir: Performed load testing and asked to gate the signing call with a sampled sampling rate for high-traffic tenants; author added a sampling config with conservative defaults.\\nFinal: All reviewers approved, security review signed off pending key-rotation guidance added to docs.\",\n  \"merge_method\": \"squash\",\n  \"merged_by\": \"Lucia Gomez\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"- Introduce Residency Assertor for deterministic tenant-region recommendations.\\n- Add Audit Commitment Gateway for signed, non-repudiable records when requests are routed off-region.\\n- New operator KMS allowlist and selection policy.\\n- Helm values for residency and migration backfill script.\\n\\nOperators: enable via feature flag residency_assertor_v1 and follow the observe-only rollout documented in docs/security/kms-residency.md.\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_comments\",\n    \"release_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: redwood\n\ncommitment gateway \" that signs short commitment records for any request that is routed off - region or to a fallback key. what it does : adds a residency assertor that derives a tenant region preference from ( in order ) tenant metadata, residency claim headers, and recent routing history ( sticky hints ). when explicit tenancy region is missing, the assertor emits a deterministic candidate list rather than a single decision to enable safe canary rollouts. kms selection now consults an allowlist and a staged preference table ; if the chosen kms is outside the tenant ' s pinned region, the request is annotated and forwarded through the audit commitment gateway, which atomically records a signed commitment ( sha256 - > operator kms sign ) and returns a short commitment id",

# EU residency failover interview notes (temporary, do not publish)

## Provisional questions

- Does the customer's executed Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum require EU-only processing as well as EU-only persistence, or only storage/backup residency?
- Which routing mode is currently configured for the tenant: no-forward, consent-forward, or a time-bounded emergency consent?
- Is `cross_region_consent` explicitly true, and what control-plane resource version is current?
- Is the residency assertor and audit commitment gateway in enforce mode for this Hosted tenant, or only observe-only / unavailable?
- Which tenant-region KMS allowlist and preference entry is active? Is the selected key in the pinned EU region?
- Can Support retrieve the signed commitment for every off-region route or fallback-key decision?
- Are there in-flight streams that should be allowed to finish locally before failover?
- Which team owns confirmation that the Hosted production deployment matches the merged KMS-residency implementation?

## Discarded interpretations

- “EU tenancy pinning” does not by itself authorize cross-region forwarding.
- A degraded EU region does not imply consent; unknown consent is a deny.
- Nearest-region or smart-router behavior is not sufficient evidence of contractual compliance.
- A successful request or improved latency is not proof of residency.
- Cloud KMS encryption at rest does not prove that the chosen key was in the tenant's pinned region.
- The existence of signed audit commitments does not make an otherwise unconsented transfer permissible.
- The customer email's retention figures are not reused here as a general promise; the failover response must not invent or generalize retention terms.

## Follow-ups

- Legal/Account: confirm the executed addendum and any explicit cross-region terms.
- Platform/SRE: confirm Hosted production feature flags, tenant residency assertion, KMS allowlist, selected key region, and audit commitment health.
- Security/Compliance: confirm who may access the RBAC-protected commitment verification endpoint and what evidence can be shared.
- Support: capture request IDs, timestamps, routing headers, router/API-gateway traces, consent state, and commitment IDs; do not request customer payloads unless separately required and approved.

# Hosted API EU residency failover response

## Purpose and reviewed support rule

For a Hosted Enterprise tenant pinned to the EU, Support must treat the executed data-residency addendum and the tenant's current control-plane state as authoritative. Cross-region forwarding is allowed only when explicit tenant consent is present. Missing, unknown, or unverified consent is a deny: keep traffic in-region or return the residency hold response, then escalate. Never describe a regional outage, proximity routing, or emergency as implicit consent.

## Contract boundary

Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy's primary region. EU-only tenancy pinning is available under the Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum. For EU-only contracts, cross-region backup replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted. These facts establish the contract boundary, but the executed customer terms must be checked before answering a specific customer. This runbook makes no additional retention, deletion, availability, or timing promise.

Evidence: [Hosted API security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`).

## Supported routing modes

- **No-forward:** traffic remains in the pinned EU region. If the local route cannot serve, fail closed with the residency hold/error response rather than proxying outside the region.
- **Consent-forward:** drain and proxy to a fallback region only when the tenant control plane has `cross_region_consent = true`. Without that exact affirmative state, return `409` with `Retry-After` and emit the operator signal.
- **Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.
- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.

Residency decision headers are `X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal` and `X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown`. `unknown` defaults to deny. Use the tenant resource version when changing state to avoid races.

Evidence: [Architecture residency swap decision](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/architecture/3478920001-residency-swap-assertor-notes.json) (`dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498`).

## KMS and audit behavior

Encryption at rest uses cloud KMS by default for Hosted API; customer-managed key options depend on the enterprise terms. Runtime KMS selection must consult the operator KMS allowlist and staged preference policy. If a fallback key is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and passed through the audit commitment gateway.

For an off-region route or fallback-key selection, the gateway records a signed commitment using a dedicated operator-KMS signing key. The commitment contains a timestamp, request hash, and origin region; the audit forwarder retains the commitment ID and can retrieve the signed record. Verification access is RBAC-protected. A commitment is evidence of the decision, not consent and not permission to override the contract.

Before relying on this behavior for a Hosted customer, verify the production tenant has the residency assertor/gateway enabled in enforce mode, the allowlist is seeded, and the signer/forwarder is healthy. The merged implementation documents an observe-only rollout path, so code availability alone is not proof of tenant enforcement.

Evidence: [Merged KMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).

## Support validation steps

1. Confirm tenant identity, the pinned region, and the executed residency addendum; identify any explicit cross-region clause.
2. Capture request IDs, UTC timestamps, endpoint/model, and customer-visible routing/residency headers. Avoid collecting payload content unless separately necessary and approved.
3. Check `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy` in logs. Correlate smart-router decisions with API-gateway connection traces to determine whether proxying occurred.
4. Read the current control-plane `cross_region_consent`, residency mode/decision, emergency-consent expiry and approvals, and tenant resource version. Treat absent or unknown values as deny.
5. Verify the effective KMS key is allowlisted and region-compatible with the tenant pin. For any fallback key or off-region route, capture the audit commitment ID and verify the signed commitment through the authorized endpoint.
6. Check for pinned in-flight streams and confirm they were allowed to finish locally.
7. State only what the evidence proves: configured contract boundary, observed route, consent state, KMS/key-region result, and audit artifact availability.
8. If a misroute is confirmed, preserve routing/API-gateway evidence, pin the EU route where authorized, engage the incident process, and coordinate the reviewed customer response with Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance.

The incident record demonstrates the expected diagnostic pattern: inspect `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy`, correlate router and gateway traces, and mitigate confirmed locality failures by pinning EU routes and rolling back the routing-weight change.

Evidence: [SUP-7813 EU cross-region routing incident](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`).

## Escalate immediately when

- the executed addendum or cross-region clause is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent with tenant configuration;
- consent is absent, unknown, expired, or changed without the required approvals;
- an EU-pinned request was routed or persisted outside the allowed region without explicit consent;
- the effective KMS key is outside policy, the allowlist/pin cannot be verified, or the signing gateway is unavailable;
- an expected audit commitment is missing or cannot be verified;
- routing headers conflict with router, gateway, KMS, or audit evidence;
- Support is asked to promise retention, deletion, availability, or a response date not stated in the customer's executed terms.

## Customer-facing response pattern

“Your Hosted Enterprise residency terms and the tenant's current configuration govern failover. We do not treat an outage as permission to transfer traffic. Cross-region forwarding requires an explicit allowed consent state; missing or unknown consent fails closed. We are validating the observed route, consent state, effective KMS region, and signed audit evidence. If any item conflicts with your executed terms, we will escalate to Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance and provide only verified findings.”

## Uncertainty

The sources establish the Hosted contract boundary, the architecture consent defaults, a merged KMS/audit implementation, and Support's observed routing diagnostics. They do not by themselves prove that every Hosted production tenant has the residency assertor and commitment gateway enabled in enforce mode, nor do they replace a customer's executed addendum. Support must verify both before making a definitive compliance statement.

# Hosted API EU residency failover response

## Purpose and reviewed support rule

For a Hosted Enterprise tenant pinned to the EU, Support must treat the executed data-residency addendum and the tenant's current control-plane state as authoritative. Cross-region forwarding is allowed only when explicit tenant consent is present. Missing, unknown, or unverified consent is a deny: keep traffic in-region or return the residency hold response, then escalate. Never describe a regional outage, proximity routing, or emergency as implicit consent.

## Contract boundary

Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy's primary region. EU-only tenancy pinning is available under the Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum. For EU-only contracts, cross-region backup replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted. These facts establish the contract boundary, but the executed customer terms must be checked before answering a specific customer. This runbook makes no additional retention, deletion, availability, or timing promise.

Evidence: [Hosted API security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`).

## Supported routing modes

- **No-forward:** traffic remains in the pinned EU region. If the local route cannot serve, fail closed with the residency hold/error response rather than proxying outside the region.
- **Consent-forward:** drain and proxy to a fallback region only when the tenant control plane has `cross_region_consent = true`. Without that exact affirmative state, return `409` with `Retry-After` and emit the operator signal.
- **Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.
- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.

Residency decision headers are `X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal` and `X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown`. `unknown` defaults to deny. Use the tenant resource version when changing state to avoid races.

Evidence: [Architecture residency swap decision](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/architecture/3478920001-residency-swap-assertor-notes.json) (`dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498`).

## KMS and audit behavior

Encryption at rest uses cloud KMS by default for Hosted API; customer-managed key options depend on the enterprise terms. Runtime KMS selection must consult the operator KMS allowlist and staged preference policy. If a fallback key is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and passed through the audit commitment gateway.

For an off-region route or fallback-key selection, the gateway records a signed commitment using a dedicated operator-KMS signing key. The commitment contains a timestamp, request hash, and origin region; the audit forwarder retains the commitment ID and can retrieve the signed record. Verification access is RBAC-protected. A commitment is evidence of the decision, not consent and not permission to override the contract.

Before relying on this behavior for a Hosted customer, verify the production tenant has the residency assertor/gateway enabled in enforce mode, the allowlist is seeded, and the signer/forwarder is healthy. The merged implementation documents an observe-only rollout path, so code availability alone is not proof of tenant enforcement.

Evidence: [Merged KMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).

## Support validation steps

1. Confirm tenant identity, the pinned region, and the executed residency addendum; identify any explicit cross-region clause.
2. Capture request IDs, UTC timestamps, endpoint/model, and customer-visible routing/residency headers. Avoid collecting payload content unless separately necessary and approved.
3. Check `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy` in logs. Correlate smart-router decisions with API-gateway connection traces to determine whether proxying occurred.
4. Read the current control-plane `cross_region_consent`, residency mode/decision, emergency-consent expiry and approvals, and tenant resource version. Treat absent or unknown values as deny.
5. Verify the effective KMS key is allowlisted and region-compatible with the tenant pin. For any fallback key or off-region route, capture the audit commitment ID and verify the signed commitment through the authorized endpoint.
6. Check for pinned in-flight streams and confirm they were allowed to finish locally.
7. State only what the evidence proves: configured contract boundary, observed route, consent state, KMS/key-region result, and audit artifact availability.
8. If a misroute is confirmed, preserve routing/API-gateway evidence, pin the EU route where authorized, engage the incident process, and coordinate the reviewed customer response with Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance.

The incident record demonstrates the expected diagnostic pattern: inspect `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy`, correlate router and gateway traces, and mitigate confirmed locality failures by pinning EU routes and rolling back the routing-weight change.

Evidence: [SUP-7813 EU cross-region routing incident](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`).

## Escalate immediately when

- the executed addendum or cross-region clause is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent with tenant configuration;
- consent is absent, unknown, expired, or changed without the required approvals;
- an EU-pinned request was routed or persisted outside the allowed region without explicit consent;
- the effective KMS key is outside policy, the allowlist/pin cannot be verified, or the signing gateway is unavailable;
- an expected audit commitment is missing or cannot be verified;
- routing headers conflict with router, gateway, KMS, or audit evidence;
- Support is asked to promise retention, deletion, availability, or a response date not stated in the customer's executed terms.

## Customer-facing response pattern

“Your Hosted Enterprise residency terms and the tenant's current configuration govern failover. We do not treat an outage as permission to transfer traffic. Cross-region forwarding requires an explicit allowed consent state; missing or unknown consent fails closed. We are validating the observed route, consent state, effective KMS region, and signed audit evidence. If any item conflicts with your executed terms, we will escalate to Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance and provide only verified findings.”

## Uncertainty

The sources establish the Hosted contract boundary, the architecture consent defaults, a merged KMS/audit implementation, and Support's observed routing diagnostics. They do not by themselves prove that every Hosted production tenant has the residency assertor and commitment gateway enabled in enforce mode, nor do they replace a customer's executed addendum. Support must verify both before making a definitive compliance statement.

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Reviewed Customer Support rule for Hosted EU residency failover\nSource: agent-memory\nPath: /memory/semantic_memory/reviewed-customer-support-rule-for-hosted-eu-residency-failover-22c36d34.md\nWorkspace: agent-memory\nTeam: Jada Williams\n\n# Reviewed Customer Support rule for Hosted EU residency failover\n\nMemory type: semantic_memory\nRecorded: 2026-08-01T21:38:17.706068+00:00\nConfidence: 0.96\nOwner: Jada Williams\nTags: hosted-api, eu-residency, failover, customer-support, kms, audit, reviewed\n\n## Summary\n\nFor an EU-pinned Hosted Enterprise tenant, Customer Support must validate the executed residency addendum and current tenant controls before answering. Cross-region forwarding requires explicit affirmative tenant consent; missing, unknown, or expired consent denies forwarding and fails closed.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU residency failover response\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n# Hosted API EU residency failover response\n\n## Purpose and reviewed support rule\n\nFor a Hosted Enterprise tenant pinned to the EU, Support must treat the executed data-residency addendum and the tenant's current control-plane state as authoritative. Cross-region forwarding is allowed only when explicit tenant consent is present. Missing, unknown, or unverified consent is a deny: keep traffic in-region or return the residency hold response, then escalate. Never describe a regional outage, proximity routing, or emergency as implicit consent.\n\n## Contract boundary\n\nHosted API data is persisted in the tenancy's primary region. EU-only tenancy pinning is available under the Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum. For EU-only contracts, cross-region backup replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted. These facts establish the contract boundary, but the executed customer terms must be checked before answering a specific customer. This runbook makes no additional retention, deletion, availability, or timing promise.\n\nEvidence: [Hosted API security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`).\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n- **No-forward:** traffic remains in the pinned EU region. If the local route cannot serve, fail closed with the residency hold/error response rather than proxying outside the region.\n- **Consent-forward:** drain and proxy to a fallback region only when the tenant control plane has `cross_region_consent = true`. Without that exact affirmative state, return `409` with `Retry-After` and emit the operator signal.\n- **Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.\n- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU residency failover response\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n**Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.\n- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.\n\nResidency decision headers are `X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal` and `X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown`. `unknown` defaults to deny. Use the tenant resource version when changing state to avoid races.\n\nEvidence: [Architecture residency swap decision](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/architecture/3478920001-residency-swap-assertor-notes.json) (`dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498`).\n\n## KMS and audit behavior\n\nEncryption at rest uses cloud KMS by default for Hosted API; customer-managed key options depend on the enterprise terms. Runtime KMS selection must consult the operator KMS allowlist and staged preference policy. If a fallback key is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and passed through the audit commitment gateway.\n\nFor an off-region route or fallback-key selection, the gateway records a signed commitment using a dedicated operator-KMS signing key. The commitment contains a timestamp, request hash, and origin region; the audit forwarder retains the commitment ID and can retrieve the signed record. Verification access is RBAC-protected. A commitment is evidence of the decision, not consent and not permission to override the contract.\n\nBefore relying on this behavior for a Hosted customer, verify the production tenant has the residency assertor/gateway enabled in enforce mode, the allowlist is seeded, and the signer/forwarder is healthy. The merged implementation documents an observe-only rollout path, so code availability alone is not proof of tenant enforcement.\n\nEvidence: [Merged KMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).\n\n## Support validation steps",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU residency failover response\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\nKMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).\n\n## Support validation steps\n\n1. Confirm tenant identity, the pinned region, and the executed residency addendum; identify any explicit cross-region clause.\n2. Capture request IDs, UTC timestamps, endpoint/model, and customer-visible routing/residency headers. Avoid collecting payload content unless separately necessary and approved.\n3. Check `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy` in logs. Correlate smart-router decisions with API-gateway connection traces to determine whether proxying occurred.\n4. Read the current control-plane `cross_region_consent`, residency mode/decision, emergency-consent expiry and approvals, and tenant resource version. Treat absent or unknown values as deny.\n5. Verify the effective KMS key is allowlisted and region-compatible with the tenant pin. For any fallback key or off-region route, capture the audit commitment ID and verify the signed commitment through the authorized endpoint.\n6. Check for pinned in-flight streams and confirm they were allowed to finish locally.\n7. State only what the evidence proves: configured contract boundary, observed route, consent state, KMS/key-region result, and audit artifact availability.\n8.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU residency failover response\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n[SUP-7813 EU cross-region routing incident](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`).\n\n## Escalate immediately when\n\n- the executed addendum or cross-region clause is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent with tenant configuration;\n- consent is absent, unknown, expired, or changed without the required approvals;\n- an EU-pinned request was routed or persisted outside the allowed region without explicit consent;\n- the effective KMS key is outside policy, the allowlist/pin cannot be verified, or the signing gateway is unavailable;\n- an expected audit commitment is missing or cannot be verified;\n- routing headers conflict with router, gateway, KMS, or audit evidence;\n- Support is asked to promise retention, deletion, availability, or a response date not stated in the customer's executed terms.\n\n## Customer-facing response pattern\n\n“Your Hosted Enterprise residency terms and the tenant's current configuration govern failover. We do not treat an outage as permission to transfer traffic. Cross-region forwarding requires an explicit allowed consent state; missing or unknown consent fails closed. We are validating the observed route, consent state, effective KMS region, and signed audit evidence. If any item conflicts with your executed terms, we will escalate to Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance and provide only verified findings.”\n\n## Uncertainty\n\nThe sources establish the Hosted contract boundary, the architecture consent defaults, a merged KMS/audit implementation, and Support's observed routing diagnostics. They do not by themselves prove that every Hosted production tenant has the residency assertor and commitment gateway enabled in enforce mode, nor do they replace a customer's executed addendum. Support must verify both before making a definitive compliance statement.",

            "content": "# EU residency failover interview notes (temporary, do not publish)\n\n## Provisional questions\n\n- Does the customer's executed Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum require EU-only processing as well as EU-only persistence, or only storage/backup residency?\n- Which routing mode is currently configured for the tenant: no-forward, consent-forward, or a time-bounded emergency consent?\n- Is `cross_region_consent` explicitly true, and what control-plane resource version is current?\n- Is the residency assertor and audit commitment gateway in enforce mode for this Hosted tenant, or only observe-only / unavailable?\n- Which tenant-region KMS allowlist and preference entry is active? Is the selected key in the pinned EU region?\n- Can Support retrieve the signed commitment for every off-region route or fallback-key decision?\n- Are there in-flight streams that should be allowed to finish locally before failover?\n- Which team owns confirmation that the Hosted production deployment matches the merged KMS-residency implementation?\n\n## Discarded interpretations\n\n- “EU tenancy pinning” does not by itself authorize cross-region forwarding.\n- A degraded EU region does not imply consent; unknown consent is a deny.\n- Nearest-region or smart-router behavior is not sufficient evidence of contractual compliance.\n- A successful request or improved latency is not proof of residency.\n- Cloud KMS encryption at rest does not prove that the chosen key was in the tenant's pinned region.\n- The existence of signed audit commitments does not make an otherwise unconsented transfer permissible.\n- The customer email's retention figures are not reused here as a general promise; the failover response must not invent or generalize retention terms.\n\n## Follow-ups\n\n- Legal/Account: confirm the executed addendum and any explicit cross-region terms.\n- Platform/SRE: confirm Hosted production feature flags, tenant residency assertion, KMS allowlist, selected key region, and audit commitment health.\n- Security/Compliance: confirm who may access the RBAC-protected commitment verification endpoint and what evidence can be shared.\n- Support: capture request IDs, timestamps, routing headers, router/API-gateway traces, consent state, and commitment IDs; do not request customer payloads unless separately required and approved.\n\n## Evidence consulted\n\n- Gmail — Hosted API contract response: `/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json` (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`)\n- Slack Architecture — residency swap/consent decision: `/knowledge/company/sources/slack/architecture/3478920001-residency-swap-assertor-notes.json` (`dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498`)\n- GitHub — merged KMS residency assertor and audit commitment gateway: `/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json` (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`)\n- Jira Support — EU cross-region routing incident: `/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json` (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`)\n",

            "content": "# Hosted API EU residency failover response\n\n## Purpose and reviewed support rule\n\nFor a Hosted Enterprise tenant pinned to the EU, Support must treat the executed data-residency addendum and the tenant's current control-plane state as authoritative. Cross-region forwarding is allowed only when explicit tenant consent is present. Missing, unknown, or unverified consent is a deny: keep traffic in-region or return the residency hold response, then escalate. Never describe a regional outage, proximity routing, or emergency as implicit consent.\n\n## Contract boundary\n\nHosted API data is persisted in the tenancy's primary region. EU-only tenancy pinning is available under the Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum. For EU-only contracts, cross-region backup replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted. These facts establish the contract boundary, but the executed customer terms must be checked before answering a specific customer. This runbook makes no additional retention, deletion, availability, or timing promise.\n\nEvidence: [Hosted API security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`).\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n- **No-forward:** traffic remains in the pinned EU region. If the local route cannot serve, fail closed with the residency hold/error response rather than proxying outside the region.\n- **Consent-forward:** drain and proxy to a fallback region only when the tenant control plane has `cross_region_consent = true`. Without that exact affirmative state, return `409` with `Retry-After` and emit the operator signal.\n- **Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.\n- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.\n\nResidency decision headers are `X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal` and `X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown`. `unknown` defaults to deny. # Hosted API EU residency failover response

## Purpose and reviewed support rule

For a Hosted Enterprise tenant pinned to the EU, Support must treat the executed data-residency addendum and the tenant's current control-plane state as authoritative. Cross-region forwarding is allowed only when explicit tenant consent is present. Missing, unknown, or unverified consent is a deny: keep traffic in-region or return the residency hold response, then escalate. Never describe a regional outage, proximity routing, or emergency as implicit consent.

## Contract boundary

Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy's primary region. EU-only tenancy pinning is available under the Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum. For EU-only contracts, cross-region backup replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted. These facts establish the contract boundary, but the executed customer terms must be checked before answering a specific customer. This runbook makes no additional retention, deletion, availability, or timing promise.

Evidence: [Hosted API security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`).

## Supported routing modes

- **No-forward:** traffic remains in the pinned EU region. If the local route cannot serve, fail closed with the residency hold/error response rather than proxying outside the region.
- **Consent-forward:** drain and proxy to a fallback region only when the tenant control plane has `cross_region_consent = true`. Without that exact affirmative state, return `409` with `Retry-After` and emit the operator signal.
- **Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.
- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.

**Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.
- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.

Residency decision headers are `X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal` and `X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown`. `unknown` defaults to deny. Use the tenant resource version when changing state to avoid races.

Evidence: [Architecture residency swap decision](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/architecture/3478920001-residency-swap-assertor-notes.json) (`dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498`).

## KMS and audit behavior

Encryption at rest uses cloud KMS by default for Hosted API; customer-managed key options depend on the enterprise terms. Runtime KMS selection must consult the operator KMS allowlist and staged preference policy. If a fallback key is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and passed through the audit commitment gateway.

For an off-region route or fallback-key selection, the gateway records a signed commitment using a dedicated operator-KMS signing key. The commitment contains a timestamp, request hash, and origin region; the audit forwarder retains the commitment ID and can retrieve the signed record. Verification access is RBAC-protected. A commitment is evidence of the decision, not consent and not permission to override the contract.

Before relying on this behavior for a Hosted customer, verify the production tenant has the residency assertor/gateway enabled in enforce mode, the allowlist is seeded, and the signer/forwarder is healthy. The merged implementation documents an observe-only rollout path, so code availability alone is not proof of tenant enforcement.

Evidence: [Merged KMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).

## Support validation steps

## Support validation steps

1. Confirm tenant identity, the pinned region, and the executed residency addendum; identify any explicit cross-region clause.
2. Capture request IDs, UTC timestamps, endpoint/model, and customer-visible routing/residency headers. Avoid collecting payload content unless separately necessary and approved.
3. Check `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy` in logs. Correlate smart-router decisions with API-gateway connection traces to determine whether proxying occurred.
4. Read the current control-plane `cross_region_consent`, residency mode/decision, emergency-consent expiry and approvals, and tenant resource version. Treat absent or unknown values as deny.
5. Verify the effective KMS key is allowlisted and region-compatible with the tenant pin. For any fallback key or off-region route, capture the audit commitment ID and verify the signed commitment through the authorized endpoint.
6. Check for pinned in-flight streams and confirm they were allowed to finish locally.
7. State only what the evidence proves: configured contract boundary, observed route, consent state, KMS/key-region result, and audit artifact availability.

## Provisional questions

- Does the customer's executed Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum require EU-only processing as well as EU-only persistence, or only storage/backup residency?

- Can Support retrieve the signed commitment for every off-region route or fallback-key decision?
- Are there in-flight streams that should be allowed to finish locally before failover?
- Which team owns confirmation that the Hosted production deployment matches the merged KMS-residency implementation?

## Discarded interpretations

- “EU tenancy pinning” does not by itself authorize cross-region forwarding.
- A degraded EU region does not imply consent; unknown consent is a deny.
- Nearest-region or smart-router behavior is not sufficient evidence of contractual compliance.
- A successful request or improved latency is not proof of residency.
- Cloud KMS encryption at rest does not prove that the chosen key was in the tenant's pinned region.
- The existence of signed audit commitments does not make an otherwise unconsented transfer permissible.
- The customer email's retention figures are not reused here as a general promise; the failover response must not invent or generalize retention terms.

## Follow-ups

- Legal/Account: confirm the executed addendum and any explicit cross-region terms.
- Platform/SRE: confirm Hosted production feature flags, tenant residency assertion, KMS allowlist, selected key region, and audit commitment health.
- Security/Compliance: confirm who may access the RBAC-protected commitment verification endpoint and what evidence can be shared.
- Support: capture request IDs, timestamps, routing headers, router/API-gateway traces, consent state, and commitment IDs; do not request customer payloads unless separately required and approved.

# Hosted API EU residency failover response

## Purpose and reviewed support rule

For a Hosted Enterprise tenant pinned to the EU, Support must treat the executed data-residency addendum and the tenant's current control-plane state as authoritative. Cross-region forwarding is allowed only when explicit tenant consent is present. Missing, unknown, or unverified consent is a deny: keep traffic in-region or return the residency hold response, then escalate. Never describe a regional outage, proximity routing, or emergency as implicit consent.

## Contract boundary

Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy's primary region. EU-only tenancy pinning is available under the Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum. For EU-only contracts, cross-region backup replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted. These facts establish the contract boundary, but the executed customer terms must be checked before answering a specific customer. This runbook makes no additional retention, deletion, availability, or timing promise.

Evidence: [Hosted API security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`).

## Supported routing modes

- **No-forward:** traffic remains in the pinned EU region. If the local route cannot serve, fail closed with the residency hold/error response rather than proxying outside the region.
- **Consent-forward:** drain and proxy to a fallback region only when the tenant control plane has `cross_region_consent = true`. Without that exact affirmative state, return `409` with `Retry-After` and emit the operator signal.
- **Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.
- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.

Residency decision headers are `X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal` and `X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown`. `unknown` defaults to deny. Use the tenant resource version when changing state to avoid races.

Evidence: [Architecture residency swap decision](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/architecture/3478920001-residency-swap-assertor-notes.json) (`dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498`).

## KMS and audit behavior

Encryption at rest uses cloud KMS by default for Hosted API; customer-managed key options depend on the enterprise terms. Runtime KMS selection must consult the operator KMS allowlist and staged preference policy. If a fallback key is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and passed through the audit commitment gateway.

For an off-region route or fallback-key selection, the gateway records a signed commitment using a dedicated operator-KMS signing key. The commitment contains a timestamp, request hash, and origin region; the audit forwarder retains the commitment ID and can retrieve the signed record. Verification access is RBAC-protected. A commitment is evidence of the decision, not consent and not permission to override the contract.

Before relying on this behavior for a Hosted customer, verify the production tenant has the residency assertor/gateway enabled in enforce mode, the allowlist is seeded, and the signer/forwarder is healthy. The merged implementation documents an observe-only rollout path, so code availability alone is not proof of tenant enforcement.

Evidence: [Merged KMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).

## Support validation steps

1. Confirm tenant identity, the pinned region, and the executed residency addendum; identify any explicit cross-region clause.
2. Capture request IDs, UTC timestamps, endpoint/model, and customer-visible routing/residency headers. Avoid collecting payload content unless separately necess

ary and approved.
3. Check `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy` in logs. Correlate smart-router decisions with API-gateway connection traces to determine whether proxying occurred.
4. Read the current control-plane `cross_region_consent`, residency mode/decision, emergency-consent expiry and approvals, and tenant resource version. Treat absent or unknown values as deny.
5. Verify the effective KMS key is allowlisted and region-compatible with the tenant pin. For any fallback key or off-region route, capture the audit commitment ID and verify the signed commitment through the authorized endpoint.
6. Check for pinned in-flight streams and confirm they were allowed to finish locally.
7. State only what the evidence proves: configured contract boundary, observed route, consent state, KMS/key-region result, and audit artifact availability.
8. If a misroute is confirmed, preserve routing/API-gateway evidence, pin the EU route where authorized, engage the incident process, and coordinate the reviewed customer response with Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance.

The incident record demonstrates the expected diagnostic pattern: inspect `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy`, correlate router and gateway traces, and mitigate confirmed locality failures by pinning EU routes and rolling back the routing-weight change.

Evidence: [SUP-7813 EU cross-region routing incident](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`).

## Escalate immediately when

- the executed addendum or cross-region clause is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent with tenant configuration;
- consent is absent, unknown, expired, or changed without the required approvals;
- an EU-pinned request was routed or persisted outside the allowed region without explicit consent;
- the effective KMS key is outside policy, the allowlist/pin cannot be verified, or the signing gateway is unavailable;
- an expected audit commitment is missing or cannot be verified;
- routing headers conflict with router, gateway, KMS, or audit evidence;
- Support is asked to promise retention, deletion, availability, or a response date not stated in the customer's executed terms.

## Customer-facing response pattern

“Your Hosted Enterprise residency terms and the tenant's current configuration govern failover. We do not treat an outage as permission to transfer traffic. Cross-region forwarding requires an explicit allowed consent state; missing or unknown consent fails closed. We are validating the observed route, consent state, effective KMS region, and signed audit evidence. If any item conflicts with your executed terms, we will escalate to Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance and provide only verified findings.”

## Uncertainty

The sources establish the Hosted contract boundary, the architecture consent defaults, a merged KMS/audit implementation, and Support's observed routing diagnostics. They do not by themselves prove that every Hosted production tenant has the residency assertor and commitment gateway enabled in enforce mode, nor do they replace a customer's executed addendum. Support must verify both before making a definitive compliance statement.

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU residency failover response\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n**Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.\n- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.\n\nResidency decision headers are `X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal` and `X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown`. `unknown` defaults to deny. Use the tenant resource version when changing state to avoid races.\n\nEvidence: [Architecture residency swap decision](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/architecture/3478920001-residency-swap-assertor-notes.json) (`dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498`).\n\n## KMS and audit behavior\n\nEncryption at rest uses cloud KMS by default for Hosted API; customer-managed key options depend on the enterprise terms. Runtime KMS selection must consult the operator KMS allowlist and staged preference policy. If a fallback key is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and passed through the audit commitment gateway.\n\nFor an off-region route or fallback-key selection, the gateway records a signed commitment using a dedicated operator-KMS signing key. The commitment contains a timestamp, request hash, and origin region; the audit forwarder retains the commitment ID and can retrieve the signed record. Verification access is RBAC-protected. A commitment is evidence of the decision, not consent and not permission to override the contract.\n\nBefore relying on this behavior for a Hosted customer, verify the production tenant has the residency assertor/gateway enabled in enforce mode, the allowlist is seeded, and the signer/forwarder is healthy. The merged implementation documents an observe-only rollout path, so code availability alone is not proof of tenant enforcement.\n\nEvidence: [Merged KMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).\n\n## Support validation steps",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU residency failover response\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\nKMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).\n\n## Support validation steps\n\n1. Confirm tenant identity, the pinned region, and the executed residency addendum; identify any explicit cross-region clause.\n2. Capture request IDs, UTC timestamps, endpoint/model, and customer-visible routing/residency headers. Avoid collecting payload content unless separately necessary and approved.\n3. Check `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy` in logs. Correlate smart-router decisions with API-gateway connection traces to determine whether proxying occurred.\n4. Read the current control-plane `cross_region_consent`, residency mode/decision, emergency-consent expiry and approvals, and tenant resource version. Treat absent or unknown values as deny.\n5. Verify the effective KMS key is allowlisted and region-compatible with the tenant pin. For any fallback key or off-region route, capture the audit commitment ID and verify the signed commitment through the authorized endpoint.\n6. Check for pinned in-flight streams and confirm they were allowed to finish locally.\n7. State only what the evidence proves: configured contract boundary, observed route, consent state, KMS/key-region result, and audit artifact availability.\n8.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU residency failover response\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-williams/eu-residency-runbook-v3\n\n[SUP-7813 EU cross-region routing incident](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`).\n\n## Escalate immediately when\n\n- the executed addendum or cross-region clause is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent with tenant configuration;\n- consent is absent, unknown, expired, or changed without the required approvals;\n- an EU-pinned request was routed or persisted outside the allowed region without explicit consent;\n- the effective KMS key is outside policy, the allowlist/pin cannot be verified, or the signing gateway is unavailable;\n- an expected audit commitment is missing or cannot be verified;\n- routing headers conflict with router, gateway, KMS, or audit evidence;\n- Support is asked to promise retention, deletion, availability, or a response date not stated in the customer's executed terms.\n\n## Customer-facing response pattern\n\n“Your Hosted Enterprise residency terms and the tenant's current configuration govern failover. We do not treat an outage as permission to transfer traffic. Cross-region forwarding requires an explicit allowed consent state; missing or unknown consent fails closed. document.title: Hosted API EU residency failover response
document.content:
# Hosted API EU residency failover response

## Purpose and reviewed support rule

For a Hosted Enterprise tenant pinned to the EU, Support must treat the executed data-residency addendum and the tenant's current control-plane state as authoritative. Cross-region forwarding is allowed only when explicit tenant consent is present. Missing, unknown, or unverified consent is a deny: keep traffic in-region or return the residency hold response, then escalate. Never describe a regional outage, proximity routing, or emergency as implicit consent.

## Contract boundary

Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy's primary region. EU-only tenancy pinning is available under the Hosted Enterprise data-residency addendum. For EU-only contracts, cross-region backup replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted. These facts establish the contract boundary, but the executed customer terms must be checked before answering a specific customer. This runbook makes no additional retention, deletion, availability, or timing promise.

Evidence: [Hosted API security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`).

## Supported routing modes

- **No-forward:** traffic remains in the pinned EU region. If the local route cannot serve, fail closed with the residency hold/error response rather than proxying outside the region.
- **Consent-forward:** drain and proxy to a fallback region only when the tenant control plane has `cross_region_consent = true`. Without that exact affirmative state, return `409` with `Retry-After` and emit the operator signal.
- **Emergency-consent:** Operations may apply a time-bounded emergency consent only with two-person approval. Support cannot infer or grant it. The approval and control-plane mutation must be auditable.
- **In-flight streaming:** allow already pinned streams to finish locally; do not silently relocate them. Mirror the relevant audit events.

Residency decision headers are `X-Residency-Mode: hold|normal` and `X-Residency-Decision: allow|deny|unknown`. `unknown` defaults to deny. Use the tenant resource version when changing state to avoid races.

Evidence: [Architecture residency swap decision](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/architecture/3478920001-residency-swap-assertor-notes.json) (`dsid_1662fb1688464890a49bd76bf984e498`).

## KMS and audit behavior

Encryption at rest uses cloud KMS by default for Hosted API; customer-managed key options depend on the enterprise terms. Runtime KMS selection must consult the operator KMS allowlist and staged preference policy. If a fallback key is outside the tenant's pinned region, the request is annotated and passed through the audit commitment gateway.

For an off-region route or fallback-key selection, the gateway records a signed commitment using a dedicated operator-KMS signing key. The commitment contains a timestamp, request hash, and origin region; the audit forwarder retains the commitment ID and can retrieve the signed record. Verification access is RBAC-protected. A commitment is evidence of the decision, not consent and not permission to override the contract.

Before relying on this behavior for a Hosted customer, verify the production tenant has the residency assertor/gateway enabled in enforce mode, the allowlist is seeded, and the signer/forwarder is healthy. The merged implementation documents an observe-only rollout path, so code availability alone is not proof of tenant enforcement.

Evidence: [Merged KMS residency and audit commitment implementation](/knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-30211-add-kms-residency-assertor-and-audit-commitment-gateway.json) (`dsid_534ff13a34e54451b1f42e14745ae8fb`).

## Support validation steps

1. Confirm tenant identity, the pinned region, and the executed residency addendum; identify any explicit cross-region clause.
2. Capture request IDs, UTC timestamps, endpoint/model, and customer-visible routing/residency headers. Avoid collecting payload content unless separately necessary and approved.
3. Check `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy` in logs. Correlate smart-router decisions with API-gateway connection traces to determine whether proxying occurred.
4. Read the current control-plane `cross_region_consent`, residency mode/decision, emergency-consent expiry and approvals, and tenant resource version. Treat absent or unknown values as deny.
5. Verify the effective KMS key is allowlisted and region-compatible with the tenant pin. For any fallback key or off-region route, capture the audit commitment ID and verify the signed commitment through the authorized endpoint.
6. Check for pinned in-flight streams and confirm they were allowed to finish locally.
7. State only what the evidence proves: configured contract boundary, observed route, consent state, KMS/key-region result, and audit artifact availability.
8. If a misroute is confirmed, preserve routing/API-gateway evidence, pin the EU route where authorized, engage the incident process, and coordinate the reviewed customer response with Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance.

The incident record demonstrates the expected diagnostic pattern: inspect `X-Region-Routed-To` and `X-Routing-Policy`, correlate router and gateway traces, and mitigate confirmed locality failures by pinning EU routes and rolling back the routing-weight change.

Evidence: [SUP-7813 EU cross-region routing incident](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`).

## Escalate immediately when

- the executed addendum or cross-region clause is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent with tenant configuration;
- consent is absent, unknown, expired, or changed without the required approvals;
- an EU-pinned request was routed or persisted outside the allowed region without explicit consent;
- the effective KMS key is outside policy, the allowlist/pin cannot be verified, or the signing gateway is unavailable;
- an expected audit commitment is missing or cannot be verified;
- routing headers conflict with router, gateway, KMS, or audit evidence;
- Support is asked to promise retention, deletion, availability, or a response date not stated in the customer's executed terms.

## Customer-facing response pattern

“Your Hosted Enterprise residency terms and the tenant's current configuration govern failover. We do not treat an outage as permission to transfer traffic. Cross-region forwarding requires an explicit allowed consent state; missing or unknown consent fails closed. We are validating the observed route, consent state, effective KMS region, and signed audit evidence. If any item conflicts with your executed terms, we will escalate to Platform/SRE and Legal/Compliance and provide only verified findings.”

## Uncertainty

The sources establish the Hosted contract boundary, the architecture consent defaults, a merged KMS/audit implementation, and Support's observed routing diagnostics. They do not by themselves prove that every Hosted production tenant has the residency assertor and commitment gateway enabled in enforce mode, nor do they replace a customer's executed addendum. Support must verify both before making a definitive compliance statement.

## Summary

For an EU-pinned Hosted Enterprise tenant, Customer Support must validate the executed residency addendum and current tenant controls before answering.
